summary: To give or bestow: 布施, dāna, the first perfection, and 施食, the feeding of hungry ghosts.
placement: Chosen by farthest-point sampling on the integrated Newton–Leipnik trajectory, so the eight stars spread across its projected shape. 魂 takes the highest of the eight points and 魄 the lowest, after the Liji’s 魂氣歸于天，形魄歸于地. A design choice, not a claim.

satellites.title: Giving While Dwelling on Nothing
satellites.evidence: 布施 renders dāna, giving, the first of the six perfections. The Diamond Sutra asks that it be done without fixing on anything: 菩薩於法應無所住行於布施 — a bodhisattva should give while dwelling on nothing.

checked.note: 菩薩於法應無所住行於布施，所謂不住色布施

satellites.title: Flaming Mouth
satellites.evidence: In Amoghavajra’s sutra, Ānanda, alone at night, sees a hungry ghost named 焰口, Flaming Mouth, 其形醜陋，身體枯瘦，口中火然: ugly, withered, fire burning in its mouth. It tells him he will die in three days unless he gives food to countless hungry ghosts, and the Buddha teaches a dhāraṇī by which one offering feeds them all.
satellites.caveat: The later rite of 放焰口 grew from this text through Song to Qing liturgies; those are not cited here.

checked.note: 見一餓鬼名曰焰口，其形醜陋，身體枯瘦，口中火然…汝過三日必當…
